sections.html:
Lane County's seat is Eugene, a city of 176,654 people in the 2020 count, up from 156,185 ten years earlier. It lies where the Willamette Valley ends, close to the McKenzie and Willamette confluence, about 110 miles from Portland and 50 from the coast.

Housing stock came to 77,395 units, 5.0 percent of them empty. Renters make up 51.6 percent of households and owners 48.4 percent, which means plenty of houses reaching the market have been rentals. Median age is 36.6.

PeaceHealth Medical Group and the University of Oregon head the employer list. When a job relocates an owner, a quick sale can become the priority.

Eugene is divided into 23 neighborhoods, from Whiteaker, Downtown and the two University districts to River Road, Santa Clara, Cal Young, Churchill, Bethel, Far West and the Southwest Hills. Skinner Butte, Spencer Butte and Mount Pisgah make the terrain uneven, and Amazon Creek runs through town.

A hillside lot near Spencer Butte raises different repair and access questions than a flat lot in Trainsong or Harlow, so describe your own setting honestly. Homes near the EmX bus line and downtown appeal to people without a car, while hillside and far west properties mean more driving.

Eugene School District 4J covers about 85 percent of the city limits and runs four full-service high schools: Churchill, North Eugene, Sheldon and South Eugene. Bethel School District serves the northwest edge. Agents look up the district for an address early, so know yours before you list.

Winters are damp and mild. A typical year brings 40.83 inches of precipitation, about 7.1 inches of snow and an average temperature of 53.1 degrees Fahrenheit. Moisture is what wears on a house here: roofs, gutters, crawl spaces, siding and decks all take a beating across the long wet season.

The weather can also swing hot. Eugene reached 111 degrees on June 27, 2021. Wildfire is a regional worry, too. The 2020 Holiday Farm Fire burned 173,393 acres in the McKenzie River valley between September 7 and October 29, 2020, and many evacuees went to nearby Springfield.

Buyers inspect closely in a climate like this. Fix or document roof leaks, soft decking and drainage trouble before an inspector finds them, and keep any smoke or fire-season notes for your insurer in one folder.

The Eugene Water & Electric Board supplies both electricity and water to more than 86,000 customers in and around the city. It is city-chartered and run by an elected five-member board. Contact EWEB before closing to schedule a final reading and the transfer of service on your sale date.

Eugene's Rental Housing Program requires registration of every rental inside city limits, rooms included, and an emergency contact who lives within 75 miles. A property outside the line is not covered, even with a Eugene mailing address.

  • Raising rent above the state maximum takes at least 90 days' notice and relocation help worth two months of rent.
  • Tenants send written notice before they file a complaint. You then get 10 days to repair the problem, or 48 hours when it involves an essential service.
  • Owners must tell the program when they sell a unit.

Inherited a rental, or done with managing one? Settle registration, open complaints and the tenant's timeline before choosing a closing date. The city's Landlord Handbook covers these duties. Selling with a tenant inside is possible, though the lease and both Oregon and Eugene notice rules stay in force. If move-out timing matters to your plan, consult a landlord-tenant attorney.

Bills are mailed by October 25. Pay it all at once or divide it into three equal parts.

Payment optionDue dateDiscount or cost
Full amountNovember 153 percent discount
Two-thirdsNovember 152 percent discount
Three equal partsNovember 15, February 15, May 15Interest at 1.333 percent a month once late

When a date falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies.

Voters approved Measure 50 in 1997 to replace Measure 47, and it holds assessed value growth to 3 percent. Lane County collects the tax for Eugene. Ask the title company to confirm payoff status before closing so any unpaid installment is cleared out of your proceeds. If the house is a rental, mention that to the title officer too, so registration and tenant paperwork are checked in the same pass.

sections.h2: What an Oregon seller must disclose
sections.html:
Once a buyer puts an offer in writing, ORS 105.464 has you hand over a written disclosure statement for covered residential property. Questions run through title and boundaries, water and sewage, structure, systems, seismic issues, flooding, settling and any other defect you know of.

After receiving the form, a buyer can back out within five days unless that right was waived. Sales by a court-appointed personal representative or by a bank after foreclosure are among the exclusions. Answers rest on your actual knowledge, so be honest. The form has no "as is" wording, and it will not protect you from a known problem you skip.

• Older houses with deferred roof, moisture or sewer-line work after years of wet winters.
  • Inherited houses where several relatives must agree and probate or a trust has to be settled first.
  • Rentals with tenants, registration paperwork and relocation rules to follow.
  • A student-driven calendar near the university, where the school year changes how fast a house moves.
  • Owners behind on payments who need a firm closing date.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html: A short folder saves days later. Pull together your latest property tax statement, any mortgage payoff figure, repair receipts and permits, and the lease if tenants live there. For a hillside house, add notes on drainage or retaining work. For a rental, add the registration confirmation from the Rental Housing Program. Inherited houses also need probate or trust papers showing who may sign.

When condition or timing is the obstacle, many owners weigh a regular listing against a direct cash sale. A cash buyer takes the house in its present state, so repairs, showings and buyer financing drop out. The title company still prepares the paperwork, prorates the property tax and clears any liens before the deed is recorded.

Before you decide, tally what a listing would cost in repairs, agent fees and months of carrying the home, then compare that to a written cash offer. We buy houses in Eugene as they are, and you can request an offer online or by phone.

faqs.a: Eugene had 176,654 residents in the 2020 census, with an estimate of 178,618 for July 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Which utility serves a Eugene house?
faqs.a: The Eugene Water & Electric Board provides both electricity and water. Call it before closing to set a final reading and transfer service to the buyer.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental house before selling it in Eugene?
faqs.a: If it is a rental inside city limits, it should be registered with the Rental Housing Program, and the program expects to hear when a unit is sold. Ask the city if you are unsure of a unit's status.

faqs.q: How long do Eugene property tax installments run?
faqs.a: Oregon bills in three parts due November 15, February 15 and May 15, with a 3 percent discount for paying in full by November 15. Interest of 1.333 percent per month applies after each due date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Eugene house with tenants living in it?
faqs.a: Yes, but the tenant's lease and the Oregon and Eugene notice rules still apply. Talk to a landlord-tenant attorney if move-out timing is part of the plan.
